doc.title: Horn Shirley — Smithsonian Jazz Oral History

title: Accompanying everyone at Shaw Junior High and winning a citywide competition
summary: At Shaw she accompanied all the singers and shows, and won a citywide competition at thirteen.

story.theme_name: Growing up and learning music: family, first instruments, teachers
story.community_name: School days: grades, teachers and leaving school

blocks.x: Did you participate in other musical activities outside of church, or outside of your studies, perhaps parties or school dances?

Child, you know one thing. When I was in school, right, see, I was in Shaw Junior High School, there was no one who could play for the specials and stuff like that, but me. I mean, I didn‘t get an education. They had to ship my ass off. I mean, this is, you know, all over the place, all over Washington. I was the one who accompanied all the singers, and the musicades, and the stuff like . . . I hope you can . . . I‘m sorry, I didn‘t mean to say [whispers] ass. But, I mean, they just used me. [laughs] I didn‘t get a decent education. They just shoved me around. ―Play for this.‖ ―Play for that.‖
How old were you when you won a citywide competition?
I was thirteen. I was thirteen.
So at that point the secret was out, and they knew who you were.
Yeah. They just shoved me on.
